annotation.authors_or_issuer: Mandl, S.; Bretschneider, M.; Meyer, S.; Gesmann-Nuissl, D.; Asbrock, F.; Meyer, B.; et al.
key_provisions_or_claims: Warmth in the Stereotype Content Model is split into Sociability and Morality to study perceptions of prosthesis users and robots.
Competence and Morality attributions to prosthesis users varied with the technical sophistication of the prosthesis.
Robots' perceived Competence was negatively related to Anthropomorphism.
Legal Personality and Decision-Making Authority attributions varied with robot Anthropomorphism.
Findings are meant to inform technology design for acceptance and to give first insights for legal treatment of anthropomorphized robots.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Two online experiments examine how people perceive prosthesis users and robots of varying anthropomorphism on Competence, Sociability and Morality. The second study also measures attributed Legal Personality and Decision-Making Authority. It offers first empirical insights for design, acceptance and the legal treatment of robots as co-workers.
annotation.title_clean: Embodied Digital Technologies: First Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
annotation.title_en: Embodied Digital Technologies: First Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
